newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close lower after setting new highs early.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close lower after setting new highs early.

text.p: Renewed selling linked to a further dip in cash pork prices and the large premium of futures to cash hog prices pushed CME hog futures sharply lower by the close after values set contract highs in April, July and August early, traders said.

Hogs closed 1.025 to 0.100 cent per lb lower paced by February at 77.650 cents. April set a new high of 77.400 cents before tumbling to close at 76.050. Pork bellies finished off 2.050 to 0.325 with February off 2.000 at 79.525 cents.
Futures tumbled when cash pork prices were quoted lower at noon, contrary to expectations the complex may be bottoming.
"The weakness in pork offset demand from the (bitter cold) weather forecast," one trader said.

Futures ran up from early lows on short covering with fund buying adding to gains in back months to set new highs. Calls for firmer cash hogs added to gains before profit taking developed and fresh selling on lower pork values pushed prices into technical sell stops. Premium of February to the index added to the setback in the nearby, they said.
The CME lean hog index fell $1.12 to $73.94 per cwt for the two days ending Jan 6, its lowest level since November 1.
Technically the market turned very weak, sources said.
"We have a major reversal in April after setting a new high and then falling and February fell below last week's low," one chartist said.

Fund rolling was also cited. Refco notably bought April and sold February which was considered the "Goldman roll". Goldman Sachs usually starts rolling its positions used in its commodity index five business days into the month.

Rand Financials and R.J. O'Brien sold February. FIMAT Futures USA bought April and June early but sold some back late. Hammer Trading and locals sold the 72/74 put spread in February options, pit sources said.
Pork bellies also fell following live hogs, with further weakness in cash bellies pressuring the market. Sell stops under early lows pushed prices sharply lower, traders said.

Bellies were weighed down early by Tuesday's bearish CME out-of-town report but recovered with hogs before again falling on selling by Rand, LFG, Cargill Investor Services and Refco, floor sources said.
CME reported a net in-movement last week of 2.85 million lbs, well above analysts' estimates of 1.0 million to 1.25 million lbs.
